phrases.reasoning: Values are spelled in lowerCamelCase and types in UpperCamelCase, so a reader tells which is which at a glance, and an underscore inside a name marks a word boundary the camel case already marks.

requireLowerCamelCaseValue.text: The {{declaration}} "{{name}}" is a value, so spell it in lowerCamelCase: "{{suggestion}}". <<reasoning>>

requireUpperCamelCaseType.text: The {{declaration}} "{{name}}" is a type, so spell it in UpperCamelCase: "{{suggestion}}". <<reasoning>>

requireUpperCamelCaseCapital.text: The {{declaration}} "{{name}}" keeps its capital, as a component, a constructor or a decorator does, so spell it in UpperCamelCase: "{{suggestion}}". <<reasoning>>

noLeadingUnderscore.text: The {{declaration}} "{{name}}" opens with an underscore; spell it "{{suggestion}}". A leading underscore is a convention for private or for unused, and TypeScript says private with `#` or the `private` modifier, which the compiler checks. A name nothing reads is deleted, or written as the bare `_` where its position has to be held.
